name: Dhanteras
description: Dhanteras marks the first day of the five-day Diwali festival, observed on Kartik Krishna Trayodashi. It honours Lord Dhanvantari, the divine physician, and Goddess Lakshmi, and is the traditional day to invite prosperity into the home.
significance: According to the Puranas, Lord Dhanvantari emerged from the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan) on this day holding the pot of amrit. Families purchase new metal utensils, gold or silver as an auspicious beginning, and light a Yama Deepam at the doorstep in the evening for the protection of the household.
puja_guidance: Clean the home and decorate the entrance with rangoli. In the evening, during Pradosh Kaal, worship Lord Dhanvantari, Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Kubera. Offer flowers, sweets and a ghee diya. Light a four-faced Yama Deepam facing south at the main door after sunset.
dos:
Clean and decorate the home
Buy a new metal utensil, gold or silver if possible
Light a Yama Deepam facing south after sunset
Worship Lakshmi, Kubera and Dhanvantari in Pradosh Kaal
Donate food or clothes to the needy
donts:
Do not lend money on this day
Avoid buying sharp objects or black items
Do not leave the home dark after sunset
Avoid quarrels and harsh words
seo_title: Dhanteras: Date, Puja Vidhi, Muhurat & Significance
seo_description: Dhanteras date, Lakshmi-Kubera-Dhanvantari puja vidhi, Yama Deepam ritual, mantra and do's and don'ts for the first day of Diwali.

name: Narak Chaturdashi
description: Narak Chaturdashi, also called Choti Diwali or Roop Chaudas, celebrates Lord Krishna's victory over the demon Narakasura. It is a day of purification before the main Diwali night.
significance: Lord Krishna, with Satyabhama, defeated Narakasura and freed the captives held by him. The early-morning Abhyang Snan (oil bath) before sunrise is believed to cleanse negativity, and lamps are lit to drive away darkness.
puja_guidance: Wake before sunrise and take an oil bath (Abhyang Snan) with ubtan. Worship Lord Krishna and Yamaraj. In the evening, light diyas around the home, especially near the entrance and water sources.
dos:
Take an oil bath before sunrise
Light diyas in every corner of the home
Worship Lord Krishna and Yamaraj
Wear clean, new clothes
donts:
Do not sleep late on this morning
Avoid non-vegetarian food and alcohol
Do not leave the home unlit in the evening
seo_title: Narak Chaturdashi (Choti Diwali): Date, Abhyang Snan & Puja
seo_description: Narak Chaturdashi date, Abhyang Snan timing, Krishna and Yama puja vidhi, mantra and traditions of Choti Diwali.

name: Diwali (Lakshmi Puja)
description: Diwali, the festival of lights, is celebrated on Kartik Amavasya. It is the most important night for Lakshmi Puja, when Goddess Lakshmi is welcomed into clean, lit homes for prosperity and well-being.
significance: Diwali celebrates Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya after fourteen years of exile and the victory of light over darkness. On this Amavasya night, Goddess Lakshmi is believed to visit homes that are clean, bright and devoted. Ganesha is worshipped first for an obstacle-free year.
puja_guidance: Clean the home fully and draw rangoli at the entrance. In the Pradosh Kaal / Sthir Lagna muhurat, set up an altar with Ganesha and Lakshmi on a red cloth. Offer kumkum, rice, flowers, sweets, a coin and a ghee diya. Recite the Lakshmi mantra and Shri Suktam, then perform aarti. Keep a lamp burning through the night.
dos:
Clean the home and light diyas everywhere
Worship Ganesha first, then Lakshmi
Perform puja in the muhurat (Pradosh Kaal)
Keep the main door open during Lakshmi Puja
Share sweets with family and neighbours
donts:
Do not leave the home unclean or dark
Avoid gambling and alcohol
Do not quarrel or speak harshly
Avoid sleeping immediately after puja
seo_title: Diwali Lakshmi Puja: Date, Muhurat, Puja Vidhi & Mantra
seo_description: Diwali date, Lakshmi Puja muhurat, step-by-step Ganesh-Lakshmi puja vidhi, mantra, do's and don'ts for the festival of lights.

name: Govardhan Puja
description: Govardhan Puja, also called Annakut, is celebrated the day after Diwali. It honours Lord Krishna, who lifted the Govardhan hill to protect the people of Vrindavan.
significance: When Indra sent torrential rain over Vraj, Lord Krishna lifted Govardhan hill on his little finger for seven days, sheltering every person and cow. The festival teaches gratitude to nature and surrender to the Lord. A mountain of food (Annakut) is offered.
puja_guidance: Make a small Govardhan hill from cow dung or clay in the courtyard and decorate it with flowers. Offer Annakut, a large variety of vegetarian dishes, to Lord Krishna. Perform parikrama of the Govardhan model and worship cows.
dos:
Offer Annakut (many dishes) to Lord Krishna
Worship cows and feed them
Perform parikrama of the Govardhan model
Share prasad with everyone
donts:
Avoid non-vegetarian food
Do not waste food
Avoid disrespecting cows or nature
seo_title: Govardhan Puja (Annakut): Date, Puja Vidhi & Story
seo_description: Govardhan Puja date, Annakut offering, puja vidhi, mantra and the story of Krishna lifting Govardhan hill.

name: Bhai Dooj
description: Bhai Dooj, also called Yama Dwitiya, celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters perform tilak and pray for their brothers' long life and well-being.
significance: Yamaraj visited his sister Yamuna on this day, who welcomed him with tilak and a meal. Pleased, Yama blessed that any brother who receives tilak from his sister on this day is protected from untimely fear.
puja_guidance: The sister prepares a thali with roli, rice, a diya and sweets. She applies tilak to her brother, performs aarti and offers sweets. The brother gives a gift and promises protection. Many also offer prayers to Yamaraj and Yamuna.
dos:
Sisters apply tilak and perform aarti for brothers
Brothers visit their sisters and give a gift
Share a meal together
Pray for each other's well-being
donts:
Avoid quarrels between siblings
Do not skip the tilak in the auspicious muhurat
Avoid non-vegetarian food
seo_title: Bhai Dooj: Date, Tilak Muhurat, Puja Vidhi & Story
seo_description: Bhai Dooj date, tilak muhurat, puja thali and vidhi, and the story of Yama and Yamuna.

name: Chhath Puja
description: Chhath Puja is a four-day festival dedicated to Surya Dev and Chhathi Maiya, observed on Kartik Shukla Shashthi. Devotees offer arghya to the setting and rising sun from riverbanks and ponds.
significance: Chhath is one of the oldest Vedic sun-worship traditions, especially in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh. Devotees observe a strict nirjala fast and thank Surya Dev for life and health, praying for the well-being of the family.
puja_guidance: Day 1 Nahay Khay: bath and a pure sattvik meal. Day 2 Kharna: fast through the day and eat kheer in the evening. Day 3: offer evening arghya to the setting sun standing in water. Day 4: offer morning arghya to the rising sun, then break the fast with prasad (thekua, fruits).
dos:
Maintain complete cleanliness and purity
Offer arghya to the setting and rising sun
Prepare prasad like thekua at home
Sing Chhath geet with family
donts:
Do not use onion, garlic or non-vegetarian food
Do not touch prasad without bathing
Avoid breaking the fast before the morning arghya
seo_title: Chhath Puja: Dates, Arghya Timings, Rituals & Vidhi
seo_description: Chhath Puja four-day dates, sunset and sunrise arghya rituals, Nahay Khay and Kharna, prasad and puja vidhi.

name: Ahoi Ashtami
description: Ahoi Ashtami is a fast kept by mothers on Kartik Krishna Ashtami for the long life and well-being of their children. The fast is broken after sighting the stars in the evening.
significance: Mothers worship Ahoi Mata (a form of Parvati) and pray for their children's protection. The tradition recalls a mother whose sincere repentance and devotion to Ahoi Mata restored blessings to her family.
puja_guidance: Draw or place an image of Ahoi Mata on the wall. In the evening, offer water, roli, rice, sweets and a diya, and listen to the Ahoi Ashtami katha. Offer arghya to the stars and then break the fast.
dos:
Keep the fast from sunrise until the stars appear
Listen to the Ahoi Mata katha
Offer arghya to the stars
Bless children after the puja
donts:
Avoid digging soil or using sharp tools
Do not break the fast before seeing the stars
Avoid harsh words with children
seo_title: Ahoi Ashtami Vrat: Date, Puja Vidhi, Katha & Star Sighting
seo_description: Ahoi Ashtami date, puja vidhi, katha and star-sighting time for the mothers' fast for children.

name: Rama Ekadashi
description: Rama Ekadashi falls on Kartik Krishna Ekadashi, just before Diwali. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi (Rama), and is believed to bring prosperity and remove past karma.
significance: The Padma Purana describes Rama Ekadashi as highly meritorious. Observing this fast with devotion purifies the mind and invites the grace of Lakshmi-Narayana ahead of the Diwali season.
puja_guidance: Take a bath before sunrise and worship Lord Vishnu with Tulsi leaves, yellow flowers and a ghee diya. Recite Vishnu Sahasranama or the Ekadashi mantra. Break the fast (parana) on Dwadashi in the prescribed time.
dos:
Fast or eat only fruits and milk
Offer Tulsi leaves to Lord Vishnu
Chant Vishnu mantras and stay awake in devotion
Do parana on Dwadashi at the right time
donts:
Do not eat rice or grains
Avoid onion, garlic and non-vegetarian food
Do not pluck Tulsi leaves on Ekadashi
seo_title: Rama Ekadashi: Date, Parana Time, Vrat Vidhi & Katha
seo_description: Rama Ekadashi date, parana time, Vishnu-Lakshmi vrat vidhi, mantra and katha.

name: Dev Uthani Ekadashi
description: Dev Uthani (Prabodhini) Ekadashi falls on Kartik Shukla Ekadashi, when Lord Vishnu awakens from his four-month yoga nidra. It ends Chaturmas and reopens the season for weddings and auspicious ceremonies.
significance: Lord Vishnu rests from Devshayani Ekadashi and awakens on this day. Devotees celebrate the awakening of the Lord, and the auspicious period for marriages, griha pravesh and other samskaras begins again.
puja_guidance: Clean the home and draw the Lord's footprints at the entrance. In the evening, worship Lord Vishnu with sugarcane, seasonal fruits and Tulsi. Awaken the Lord with bells, conch and the chant 'Uttishtha Govinda'. Light diyas and keep the fast until Dwadashi parana.
dos:
Fast and worship Lord Vishnu
Offer sugarcane, fruits and Tulsi
Ring bells and chant to awaken the Lord
Light diyas in the home and at Tulsi
donts:
Do not eat rice or grains
Avoid tamasic food
Do not sleep during the evening worship
seo_title: Dev Uthani Ekadashi: Date, Parana, Puja Vidhi & Significance
seo_description: Dev Uthani (Prabodhini) Ekadashi date, parana time, Vishnu awakening puja vidhi and end of Chaturmas.

name: Tulsi Vivah
description: Tulsi Vivah is the ceremonial marriage of the sacred Tulsi plant with Lord Vishnu in the form of Shaligram. It marks the start of the Hindu wedding season.
significance: Tulsi is revered as Vrinda, a devoted form of Lakshmi. Performing Tulsi Vivah is believed to bring the merit of kanyadaan and marital harmony to the household.
puja_guidance: Decorate the Tulsi plant like a bride with a red chunri and ornaments. Place a Shaligram or Vishnu idol beside it. Perform the wedding rituals with mantras, haldi, kumkum, phere and aarti, then distribute prasad.
dos:
Decorate Tulsi as a bride
Perform the vivah rituals with family
Light a diya at the Tulsi plant
Distribute sweets as prasad
donts:
Do not pluck Tulsi leaves on this day
Avoid non-vegetarian food
Do not perform the rituals hastily
seo_title: Tulsi Vivah: Date, Muhurat, Puja Vidhi & Significance
seo_description: Tulsi Vivah date, muhurat, Tulsi-Shaligram wedding puja vidhi and its significance for the wedding season.

name: Dev Diwali
description: Dev Diwali, the Diwali of the gods, is celebrated on Kartik Purnima, most grandly on the ghats of Kashi (Varanasi), where lakhs of diyas are lit along the Ganga.
significance: Lord Shiva destroyed the demon Tripurasura on Kartik Purnima, and the gods are believed to descend to Kashi to celebrate. Lighting lamps and offering deepdaan in the Ganga on this night is considered highly meritorious.
puja_guidance: Take a holy dip or bathe with Gangajal at dawn. In the evening, light diyas at home, at the Tulsi plant and near water. Offer deepdaan by floating a diya on a river or a bowl of water, and worship Lord Shiva and Vishnu.
dos:
Bathe with Gangajal or take a holy dip
Light many diyas in the evening
Offer deepdaan for ancestors and deities
Donate lamps, food or clothes
donts:
Avoid tamasic food and alcohol
Do not leave the home dark
Avoid harsh words
seo_title: Dev Diwali (Kashi): Date, Deepdaan Timings & Significance
seo_description: Dev Diwali date, Kashi Ganga ghat deepdaan, puja vidhi and the story of Tripurasura.

name: Kartik Purnima
description: Kartik Purnima is the full moon of the holy month of Kartik, one of the most sacred days of the year for holy bathing, deepdaan and charity.
significance: The Puranas praise the Kartik Purnima snan as especially purifying. Lord Vishnu's Matsya avatar and Lord Shiva's victory over Tripurasura are both linked to this day, and charity given now is considered greatly multiplied.
puja_guidance: Take a holy bath before sunrise. Worship Lord Vishnu and Shiva, recite the Satyanarayan katha if possible, offer deepdaan in the evening and give donations of food, lamps or clothes.
dos:
Take a holy bath at dawn
Perform Satyanarayan puja or katha
Light diyas and offer deepdaan
Give charity to the needy
donts:
Avoid tamasic food
Do not skip the evening deepdaan
Avoid anger and quarrels
seo_title: Kartik Purnima: Date, Snan Muhurat, Deepdaan & Puja Vidhi
seo_description: Kartik Purnima date, holy snan time, deepdaan, Satyanarayan puja and charity traditions.

name: Utpanna Ekadashi
description: Utpanna Ekadashi falls on Margashirsha Krishna Ekadashi and marks the appearance of Goddess Ekadashi from Lord Vishnu. Devotees who wish to begin regular Ekadashi fasting traditionally start on this day.
significance: According to the Padma Purana, a divine energy (Devi Ekadashi) emerged from Lord Vishnu and defeated the demon Mura. Vishnu blessed her that anyone who fasts on Ekadashi will be freed from sins.
puja_guidance: Bathe early and worship Lord Vishnu with Tulsi, yellow flowers, fruits and a ghee diya. Read the Utpanna Ekadashi katha, chant Vishnu mantras and break the fast on Dwadashi within the parana time.
dos:
Begin the Ekadashi vrat with a sankalp
Offer Tulsi to Lord Vishnu
Read the Ekadashi katha
Do parana on Dwadashi on time
donts:
Do not eat rice or grains
Avoid onion, garlic and non-vegetarian food
Avoid gossip and anger
seo_title: Utpanna Ekadashi: Date, Parana Time, Vrat Vidhi & Katha
seo_description: Utpanna Ekadashi date, parana time, how to begin Ekadashi fasting, Vishnu puja vidhi and katha.

name: Vivah Panchami
description: Vivah Panchami celebrates the divine marriage of Lord Rama and Goddess Sita, observed on Margashirsha Shukla Panchami, with grand celebrations in Janakpur and Ayodhya.
significance: The sacred union of Sita and Rama represents ideal dharma, devotion and partnership. Worship on this day is offered for a harmonious married life and for removing obstacles in marriage.
puja_guidance: Worship idols or images of Sita and Rama, offer flowers, kumkum, sweets and a diya. Recite the Ram-Sita vivah prasang from the Ramcharitmanas and perform aarti.
dos:
Worship Sita and Rama together
Read the Ram-Sita vivah prasang
Offer sweets and flowers
Pray for harmony in married life
donts:
Avoid quarrels at home
Avoid tamasic food
Do not disrespect elders
seo_title: Vivah Panchami: Date, Ram-Sita Puja Vidhi & Significance
seo_description: Vivah Panchami date, Ram-Sita vivah puja vidhi, Ramcharitmanas path and significance for married life.

name: Mokshada Ekadashi
description: Mokshada Ekadashi falls on Margashirsha Shukla Ekadashi, the same day as Gita Jayanti. Its name means 'giver of liberation', and the fast is offered for the peace of ancestors.
significance: The Brahmanda Purana tells of King Vaikhanasa, whose father was freed from suffering by the merit of this fast. It is also celebrated in South India as Vaikuntha Ekadashi, when the gates of Vaikuntha are believed to open.
puja_guidance: Worship Lord Krishna / Vishnu with Tulsi and yellow flowers. Read or listen to the Bhagavad Gita, offer prayers for ancestors, and break the fast on Dwadashi in the parana time.
dos:
Observe the Ekadashi fast
Read the Bhagavad Gita
Pray for the peace of ancestors
Do parana on Dwadashi on time
donts:
Do not eat rice or grains
Avoid tamasic food
Avoid harsh speech
seo_title: Mokshada Ekadashi: Date, Parana Time, Vrat Vidhi & Katha
seo_description: Mokshada (Vaikuntha) Ekadashi date, parana time, vrat vidhi, Gita path and katha.

name: Gita Jayanti
description: Gita Jayanti marks the day Lord Krishna spoke the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, on Margashirsha Shukla Ekadashi.
significance: The Bhagavad Gita's 700 verses teach karma, bhakti and jnana yoga. Reading or reciting the Gita on this day is a way to honour the Lord's teaching and bring clarity to one's own life.
puja_guidance: Worship Lord Krishna and a copy of the Bhagavad Gita with flowers and a diya. Recite the Gita, or at least chapters 12 and 15, and reflect on one teaching to practise. Distribute the Gita or its message to others.
dos:
Read or listen to the Bhagavad Gita
Worship Lord Krishna
Gift a copy of the Gita
Reflect on one verse to live by
donts:
Avoid disrespecting scripture
Avoid tamasic food
Do not spend the day in idle gossip
seo_title: Gita Jayanti: Date, Significance & How to Celebrate
seo_description: Gita Jayanti date, significance, Bhagavad Gita path, Krishna puja and ways to celebrate.

name: Dattatreya Jayanti
description: Dattatreya Jayanti celebrates the birth of Lord Dattatreya, the combined form of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, observed on Margashirsha Purnima.
significance: Lord Dattatreya, son of Sage Atri and Anasuya, is revered as the Adi Guru. Worship on this day is offered for wisdom, protection and guidance from the Guru.
puja_guidance: Worship an image of Lord Dattatreya with flowers, incense and a diya. Recite the Datta mantra or Guru Charitra, and offer food to the needy and to cows.
dos:
Worship Lord Dattatreya
Recite Guru Charitra or Datta mantras
Respect your teachers and elders
Feed the needy and cows
donts:
Avoid disrespecting teachers
Avoid tamasic food
Avoid anger
seo_title: Dattatreya Jayanti: Date, Puja Vidhi & Significance
seo_description: Dattatreya Jayanti date, puja vidhi, Datta mantra and significance of the Adi Guru.

name: Margashirsha Purnima
description: Margashirsha Purnima is the full moon of Margashirsha, a month Lord Krishna calls his own in the Bhagavad Gita. It is a day for holy bathing, Satyanarayan puja and charity.
significance: Lord Krishna says 'Among months, I am Margashirsha'. Purnima of this month is considered especially auspicious for worship, fasting and giving.
puja_guidance: Take a holy bath at dawn, worship Lord Vishnu and the Moon, perform Satyanarayan katha and give charity in the evening after offering arghya to the Moon.
dos:
Take a holy bath
Perform Satyanarayan puja
Offer arghya to the Moon
Give charity
donts:
Avoid tamasic food
Avoid quarrels
Do not skip the evening prayer
seo_title: Margashirsha Purnima: Date, Vrat Vidhi & Significance
seo_description: Margashirsha Purnima date, vrat vidhi, Satyanarayan puja, Moon arghya and charity.

name: Margashirsha Amavasya
description: Margashirsha Amavasya is the new moon of Margashirsha, a traditional day for Pitru tarpan, holy bathing and charity in honour of ancestors.
significance: Amavasya is dedicated to the Pitrus. Tarpan and donations on this day are believed to bring peace to ancestors and their blessings to the family.
puja_guidance: Bathe early, offer water with black sesame (til) to ancestors facing south, light a diya under a Peepal tree in the evening and give food or clothes to the needy.
dos:
Offer tarpan to ancestors
Light a diya under a Peepal tree
Feed cows, crows and the needy
Donate food or clothes
donts:
Avoid starting new ventures
Avoid tamasic food
Do not disrespect elders
seo_title: Margashirsha Amavasya: Date, Pitru Tarpan & Rituals
seo_description: Margashirsha Amavasya date, Pitru tarpan vidhi, Peepal diya and charity rituals.

name: Vrischika Sankranti
description: Vrischika Sankranti marks the Sun's entry into Scorpio (Vrischika rashi). Sankranti days are auspicious for Surya worship, holy bathing and charity.
significance: Each Sankranti marks a change in the Sun's energy. Offering arghya to Surya and giving charity on this day is considered meritorious.
puja_guidance: Offer arghya to the rising Sun with water, red flowers and rice from a copper vessel. Recite the Aditya Hridayam or Surya mantra and donate to the needy.
dos:
Offer arghya to the Sun
Recite Surya mantras
Give charity
donts:
Avoid tamasic food
Avoid harsh speech
seo_title: Vrischika Sankranti: Date, Punya Kaal & Surya Puja
seo_description: Vrischika Sankranti date, punya kaal, Surya arghya and charity.

name: Dhanu Sankranti
description: Dhanu Sankranti marks the Sun's entry into Sagittarius (Dhanu rashi) and the start of Kharmas, a period when weddings and new ventures are traditionally paused.
significance: From Dhanu Sankranti until Makar Sankranti, the Sun is in Jupiter's sign and the period is called Kharmas. It is a time for worship, charity and spiritual practice rather than new samskaras.
puja_guidance: Offer arghya to the rising Sun, worship Lord Vishnu, recite the Surya mantra and donate warm clothes or food.
dos:
Offer arghya to the Sun
Increase worship and charity during Kharmas
Donate warm clothes
donts:
Avoid starting weddings or griha pravesh in Kharmas
Avoid tamasic food
seo_title: Dhanu Sankranti & Kharmas: Date, Significance & Rules
seo_description: Dhanu Sankranti date, start of Kharmas, Surya puja and what to avoid in Kharmas.

name: Kalabhairav Jayanti
description: Kalabhairav Jayanti celebrates the appearance of Lord Kaal Bhairav, the fierce protective form of Lord Shiva and guardian of Kashi, on Margashirsha Krishna Ashtami.
significance: Lord Kaal Bhairav is worshipped for protection from fear, negativity and obstacles. In Kashi he is honoured as the Kotwal (guardian) of the city.
puja_guidance: Worship Lord Kaal Bhairav in the evening with a mustard-oil diya, black sesame, flowers and sweets. Recite the Kalabhairav Ashtakam and feed dogs, who are considered his vahana.
dos:
Recite the Kalabhairav Ashtakam
Light a mustard-oil diya
Feed dogs
Visit a Bhairav temple
donts:
Avoid harming animals
Avoid alcohol and tamasic food
Avoid lies and harsh speech
seo_title: Kalabhairav Jayanti: Date, Puja Vidhi & Ashtakam
seo_description: Kalabhairav Jayanti date, puja vidhi, Kalabhairav Ashtakam and the guardian of Kashi.

name: Sankashti Chaturthi
description: Sankashti Chaturthi is the monthly fast for Lord Ganesha on Krishna Paksha Chaturthi. The fast is broken after offering arghya to the Moon at night.
significance: 'Sankashti' means deliverance from difficulties. Devotees fast and worship Ganesha, the remover of obstacles, for relief from troubles and success in their work.
puja_guidance: Fast through the day. In the evening, worship Lord Ganesha with durva grass, modak or laddoo, red flowers and a diya. Read the Sankashti katha, offer arghya to the Moon after moonrise and then break the fast.
dos:
Offer durva grass and modak to Ganesha
Read the Sankashti katha
Offer arghya to the Moon
Break the fast after moonrise
donts:
Do not offer Tulsi to Ganesha
Avoid tamasic food
Do not break the fast before moonrise
seo_title: Sankashti Chaturthi: Date, Moonrise Time, Vrat Vidhi & Katha
seo_description: Sankashti Chaturthi date, moonrise time, Ganesha vrat vidhi, mantra and katha.

name: Masik Shivaratri
description: Masik Shivaratri is the monthly night of Lord Shiva on Krishna Paksha Chaturdashi. Devotees fast and worship Shiva, especially at night.
significance: Each month's Shivaratri is a smaller observance of Maha Shivaratri. Regular worship on this night is believed to bring peace of mind and Shiva's grace.
puja_guidance: Fast through the day. At night, perform abhishek of the Shivlinga with water, milk and honey, offer Bilva leaves and chant Om Namah Shivaya. Many keep a vigil (jagaran) and worship in the Nishita Kaal.
dos:
Fast and worship Lord Shiva at night
Offer Bilva leaves and water to the Shivlinga
Chant Om Namah Shivaya
Keep a night vigil if possible
donts:
Do not offer Ketaki flowers or Tulsi to Shiva
Avoid tamasic food
Avoid anger
seo_title: Masik Shivaratri: Date, Nishita Kaal, Puja Vidhi & Mantra
seo_description: Masik Shivaratri date, Nishita Kaal puja time, Shiva abhishek vidhi and mantra.

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: Maha Shivaratri, the great night of Lord Shiva, is observed on Phalguna Krishna Chaturdashi. Devotees fast, keep a night-long vigil and worship Shiva through the four prahars of the night.
significance: Maha Shivaratri celebrates the union of Shiva and Shakti and the night Shiva manifested as the infinite Jyotirlinga. Worship on this night is considered the most powerful of the year for inner peace and Shiva's grace.
puja_guidance: Fast through the day. Perform abhishek of the Shivlinga in each of the four prahars with water, milk, curd, ghee, honey and sugar, offering Bilva leaves, dhatura and white flowers. Chant Om Namah Shivaya and the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra, and keep a vigil until dawn.
dos:
Fast and keep a night vigil
Perform abhishek in the four prahars
Offer Bilva leaves in sets of three
Chant the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra
donts:
Do not offer Ketaki flowers, Tulsi or kumkum to the Shivlinga
Avoid tamasic food and alcohol
Avoid sleeping through the night
seo_title: Maha Shivaratri: Date, Four Prahar Puja Timings & Vidhi
seo_description: Maha Shivaratri date, four prahar puja timings, abhishek vidhi, mantra, and do's and don'ts.

name: Holi
description: Holi, the festival of colours, is celebrated on Phalguna Purnima. Holika Dahan is lit on the evening before, and colours are played the next day to celebrate spring and the victory of devotion.
significance: Holika Dahan recalls the protection of the devotee Prahlad by Lord Vishnu, while his aunt Holika was consumed by fire. Holi celebrates Radha-Krishna's divine play and the arrival of spring.
puja_guidance: On Holika Dahan evening, worship the Holika pyre with roli, rice, flowers, raw cotton thread, coconut and new grain, then circle it while praying. The next day, offer colours to the deities first and then play with family.
dos:
Perform Holika Dahan puja in the muhurat
Offer colours to the deities first
Use natural, safe colours
Share sweets and forgive old quarrels
donts:
Avoid harmful chemical colours
Avoid alcohol and intoxicants
Do not force colours on unwilling people
seo_title: Holi & Holika Dahan: Date, Muhurat, Puja Vidhi & Story
seo_description: Holi and Holika Dahan date, muhurat, puja vidhi and the story of Prahlad and Holika.

name: Ram Navami
description: Ram Navami celebrates the birth of Lord Rama on Chaitra Shukla Navami, the last day of Chaitra Navratri. Worship is offered at the Madhyahna (midday) muhurat, the time of the Lord's birth.
significance: Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, is the ideal of dharma, truth and compassion. Ram Navami is celebrated with Ramayana path, bhajans and the ceremonial birth worship at noon.
puja_guidance: Fast or eat sattvik food. At the Madhyahna muhurat, worship Lord Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman with flowers, panchamrit, sweets and a diya. Read the Rama Janma prasang and perform aarti.
mantra: Shri Ram Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram
dos:
Worship at the Madhyahna muhurat
Read the Ramayana or Ramcharitmanas
Chant the Ram naam
Offer panakam and kosambari as prasad
donts:
Avoid tamasic food
Avoid disrespecting elders
Avoid harsh speech
seo_title: Ram Navami: Date, Madhyahna Muhurat, Puja Vidhi & Mantra
seo_description: Ram Navami date, Madhyahna puja muhurat, Rama janma puja vidhi, mantra and traditions.

name: Vasant Panchami
description: Vasant Panchami, observed on Magha Shukla Panchami, welcomes spring and honours Goddess Saraswati, the giver of knowledge, music and the arts.
significance: Students, artists and musicians worship Saraswati for wisdom and learning. Yellow, the colour of spring and of mustard fields, is worn and offered, and children often begin their first letters (Vidya Arambh) today.
puja_guidance: Wear yellow and place an image of Goddess Saraswati with books, pens and instruments. Offer yellow flowers, sweets and a diya, recite the Saraswati Vandana and seek blessings for learning.
dos:
Worship Saraswati with books and instruments
Wear and offer yellow
Begin Vidya Arambh for children
Recite Saraswati Vandana
donts:
Do not disrespect books or learning
Avoid tamasic food
Avoid quarrels
seo_title: Vasant Panchami (Saraswati Puja): Date, Muhurat & Vidhi
seo_description: Vasant Panchami date, Saraswati puja muhurat, puja vidhi, mantra and Vidya Arambh.

name: Gudi Padwa
description: Gudi Padwa is the Hindu New Year in Maharashtra, observed on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada. Families raise a Gudi, a decorated pole with a silk cloth and a copper or silver pot, at the doorstep.
significance: The Gudi symbolises victory and prosperity, and Brahma is believed to have created the universe on this day. It is an auspicious day to begin new ventures.
puja_guidance: Clean the home, draw rangoli and raise the Gudi on the right side of the main door. Worship it with flowers and sweets, and eat a mix of neem leaves and jaggery to welcome both the bitter and the sweet of the new year.
dos:
Raise the Gudi at sunrise
Draw rangoli at the entrance
Eat neem and jaggery
Begin new work or purchases
donts:
Avoid quarrels on the first day of the year
Avoid tamasic food
Do not leave the Gudi up after sunset
seo_title: Gudi Padwa: Date, Gudi Puja Vidhi & Significance
seo_description: Gudi Padwa date, how to raise and worship the Gudi, traditions and significance of the Marathi New Year.

name: Ugadi
description: Ugadi is the New Year for Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, celebrated on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada with Ugadi pachadi, oil baths and the reading of the new year's Panchang.
significance: Ugadi means the start of a new age. The six-taste Ugadi pachadi reminds us to accept life's sweet, bitter, sour, salty, spicy and tangy experiences with balance.
puja_guidance: Take an oil bath, decorate the doorway with mango leaves and rangoli, worship the family deity and prepare Ugadi pachadi. Listen to the Panchanga Shravanam (new year predictions).
dos:
Take an oil bath
Prepare Ugadi pachadi
Decorate with mango leaves
Listen to the Panchanga Shravanam
donts:
Avoid quarrels
Avoid tamasic food
Do not skip the new-year prayers
seo_title: Ugadi: Date, Puja Vidhi, Ugadi Pachadi & Significance
seo_description: Ugadi date, puja vidhi, six-taste Ugadi pachadi and Panchanga Shravanam traditions.

name: Sarva Pitru Amavasya
description: Sarva Pitru Amavasya is the last and most important day of Pitru Paksha, when shraddha can be offered for all ancestors, including those whose death date is unknown.
significance: On this day the Pitrus are believed to be closest to the earthly realm. Tarpan, shraddha and feeding Brahmins, cows, crows and dogs bring peace to ancestors and their blessings to the family.
puja_guidance: Offer tarpan with water, black sesame and kusha grass facing south. Prepare a sattvik meal for the ancestors, offer portions to a cow, crow and dog, and feed a Brahmin or the needy. Light a diya at the doorstep in the evening.
dos:
Perform tarpan and shraddha
Feed cows, crows, dogs and the needy
Light a diya facing south
Remember ancestors with gratitude
donts:
Avoid non-vegetarian food and alcohol
Avoid starting new ventures
Do not cut hair or nails
seo_title: Sarva Pitru Amavasya: Date, Shraddha & Tarpan Vidhi
seo_description: Sarva Pitru Amavasya date, shraddha and tarpan vidhi for all ancestors, and do's and don'ts.

name: Nag Panchami
description: Nag Panchami honours the Nag Devtas (serpent deities) with milk, flowers and prayers for the protection of the family.
significance: Serpents are revered in Hindu tradition as guardians and are linked to Lord Shiva and Vishnu. Worship on Nag Panchami is offered for protection and is also associated with relief from Kaal Sarp dosha.
puja_guidance: Draw or place an image of the Nag Devta, offer milk, turmeric, kumkum, flowers and sweets, and recite the Nag Gayatri. Many also worship at a Shiva temple.
dos:
Worship the Nag Devta with milk and flowers
Visit a Shiva temple
Recite the Nag Gayatri
donts:
Do not harm snakes
Avoid digging the earth on this day
Avoid cooking on an iron tawa in some traditions
seo_title: Nag Panchami: Date, Puja Vidhi & Significance
seo_description: Nag Panchami date, Nag Devta puja vidhi, mantra and significance.
